difficulty_reason: For composable morphisms f : X -> Y and g : Y -> Z of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes with h = g o f and adjoints a, b, c as in Lemma labelled lemma-twisted-inverse-image, the lemma asserts that for any K in D_QCoh(O_Z) the displayed square relating the comparison maps of equation labelled equation-compare-with-pullback is commutative, using Lh^* = Lf^* o Lg^* and c = a o b (statement lines 2188-2209). The proof abbreviates pushforwards and pullbacks and observes that the composition of the top arrows is adjoint to a map g_*f_*(f^*(g^*K otimes b(O_Z)) otimes a(O_Y)) -> K whose source is K otimes g_*f_*(f^*b(O_Z) otimes a(O_Y)) by Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-cohomology-base-change, and that the map comes from a three step composition built from the isomorphism epsilon of the same lemma, a map alpha and the counit beta of (g_*, b), tensored with the identity on K (proof lines 2211-2236). Similarly the composition of the lower horizontal arrows is adjoint to the identity on K tensored with a three step composition using a map delta whose adjoint is expressed through epsilon and alpha, and the counit gamma of (f_*, a), followed by beta (proof lines 2238-2248). The two adjoint maps agree because of the general properties of adjoint functors, adjoints and counits recalled in Categories, Section labelled categories-section-adjoint, which give gamma o f_*delta = alpha o epsilon^{-1} (proof lines 2250-2252). Translating the commutativity of the square into an identity between two adjoint maps built from counits and the base change isomorphism is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
